chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'Do not rent out the land with wheat, nor with barley, nor with dates, nor with the canal, nor with the sprouts (of water), but with gold and silver, because gold and silver are guaranteed, and these are not with a guarantee.'

key_terms.النِّطَاف: Sprouts or small amounts of water

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred currency for paying land rent in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'daman' (guarantee) in Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing between stable currency and perishable goods to mitigate gharar (uncertainty) in lease contracts. Shia scholars, particularly in the Usuli tradition, utilize this narration to argue against rent-in-kind systems, emphasizing that gold and silver serve as reliable mediums of exchange whose value is preserved, unlike crops which are subject to natural risks and variable yields.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Neither rent out the land with the wheat, nor with the barley, nor with the dates, nor with the canal, nor with the sprouts (of water), but with the gold and the silver, because the gold and the silver are guaranteed, and these are not with a guarantee’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd al-Karim from Sama‘ah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

You must not rent land in exchange for wheat, barley, dates, canals or small amount of water, but you can do so in exchange for gold or silver; gold and silver are guaranteed and those are not guaranteed.’”
